hints: For each node, count the distinct color labels in its subtree.
A subtree is a contiguous interval in Euler order, so offline queries can be sorted by right endpoint.
Maintain a Fenwick marker only at the latest occurrence of each color in the processed prefix.
analogy: Sweep the flattened tree order and leave one marker at each color's latest occurrence.
example: If a subtree interval contains red at positions 2 and 5, the marker at 5 counts red once when the query ends at 5.
algorithm: Euler-tour the tree to obtain subtree intervals. Sort nodes by tout; sweep positions, moving each color's Fenwick marker to its latest position, then query [tin,tout].
correctness: A color has exactly one marker in a subtree interval if and only if its latest occurrence before that interval's right endpoint lies inside the interval.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
